results.title: University of California, Berkeley | SAH Archipedia
results.snippet: Though Howard’s plan was never fully carried out, his architectural legacy is cemented at UC Berkeley through several projects (some erected in conjunction with the plan, others completed earlier) that offered a physical realization of President Benjamin Ide Wheeler’s dream to transform UC Berkeley into the “Athens of the West.” Howard’s design precedents at times were more Roman or Renaissance than strictly Greek, but the classical architectural language characterized several monumental buildings of reinforced concrete or stone, including the William Randolph Hearst Greek Theater in 1903, Memorial Stadium in 1923, and Sather Tower in 1914—the latter of which remains UC Berkeley’s most visible, and iconic, landmark.
